  • Rate = 151 - 220 bpm

  • Buried P waves

Treatment

  • Stable = 1st try → Vagal maneuvers
  • “Bear down”

Atrial Fibrillation

  • No P waves
  • Chaotic baseline

  • PR interval > 0.20 sec

[Mobitz I or Wenckebach]

  • PR interval progressively lengthens

Treatment

  • Often benign - monitor
  • Atropine if HR < 60 bpm & symptomatic

“Longer, longer, drop, now I have a wenckebach”

Second-Degree Type II

[Mobitz II]

  • PR interval constant - then sudden dropped QRS

Treatment

  • High risk! Can progress to 3rd degree
  • Pacemaker often needed

“If some QRS’s don’t go thru, now you have a Mobitz II”

Third Degree Heart Block

  • P waves & QRS completely dissociated

Management

  • Unstable = Emergency!
  • Transcutaneous or temporary pacing

OR

  • Temporary treatment = Dopamine infusion

“If the R’s + P’s don’t agree, now you have a 3rd degree”

  • Wide QRS > 0.12 sec

  • CPR
  • Defibrillation
  • Epinephrine 1 mg IV every 3-5 min
